entry.note: the {path:path} URL segment of GET /user_infos/...; Starlette's path convertor matches '.*', so /user_infos//C:/Windows/win.ini (or %2F-encoded) delivers path='/C:/Windows/win.ini'

guards.note: the clean version rejects any path whose stripped form starts with '/' (HTTPException 400) before the '..'/'//' regex and Path.is_absolute() checks and before lstrip('/'); the regressed version lacks it, so on Windows '/C:/Windows/win.ini' (not absolute there: no drive before the root) passes both checks and lstrip('/') returns the drive-absolute 'C:/Windows/win.ini'

sinks.note: file_path = lollmsElfServer.lollms_paths.personal_user_infos_path / path, then FileResponse(str(file_path)); pathlib discards the base directory when the right operand has a drive and root, so the response serves C:\Windows\win.ini

notes: Reviewed at 2.3 (2026-09-28). Pair: f4424cfc ('fixed vulenerability', 2024-04-04) is the direct child of 5f406b9b; the pair diff touches only lollms/security.py (+5 lines): a leading-'/' rejection at the top of sanitize_path (only when allow_absolute_path is False) and of sanitize_path_from_endpoint. The endpoint file is byte-identical at both commits (blob 92488a3f). Class: path-traversal (advisory CWE-22/CWE-29); by the code, an HTTP-supplied path is joined onto a base directory and served with FileResponse. Verified concretely by executing the real sanitize_path_from_endpoint source from each commit (stubbed HTTPException/ASCIIColors) under Windows path semantics (Python 3.12 on Windows): regressed '/C:/Windows/win.ini' -> 'C:/Windows/win.ini', and C:\Users\u\personal_data\user_infos / that = C:\Windows\win.ini; clean -> HTTPException 400. Benign names ('user.png') pass unchanged at both. Under POSIX semantics both versions already reject '/...' via Path.is_absolute(), so the regression is Windows-only, as the advisory says (the only POSIX difference is ' /x' with a leading space, which stays inside the base). HTTP delivery of a leading '/' was reasoned from Starlette routing, not executed (FastAPI is not installed here). Parallel flows closed by the same hunk but not modelled: the other ten serve_* routes in the same file (serve_bindings, serve_personalities, serve_extensions, serve_audio, serve_images, serve_outputs, serve_data, serve_help, serve_uploads, serve_discussions) follow the identical sanitize -> base / path -> FileResponse pattern. The fix's second hunk (the same check in sanitize_path) covers ~30 body-field callers in lollms_binding_infos.py, lollms_discussion.py, lollms_extensions_infos.py, lollms_personalities_infos.py, lollms_configuration_infos.py and server/events/lollms_model_events.py (several of them ignore the return value and use the raw input). sanitize_path is not on the modelled flow, so it is left out of the slice and regression.diff holds only the sanitize_path_from_endpoint hunk. Known-incomplete fix: a leading backslash ('\\Windows\\win.ini') passes both versions (is_absolute() is False on Windows, lstrip('/') ignores it, and base / it = C:\Windows\win.ini on the base's drive); 95ad36ee (2024-04-29) later closes that by replacing '\\' with '/' before the leading-slash check (separate advisories CVE-2024-4315 / CVE-2024-4881 per the 2.2 reviewers). A drive-relative 'C:Windows/win.ini' also passes both, but escapes only when the base is on another drive. The modelled flow (leading forward slash, the advisory's variant) is closed by the clean commit. In the clean version, path.strip() runs before the 'if path is None' check (a crash on None, fixed later by d577405); irrelevant here because FastAPI passes a str.
